text:
sam: FYI ran into a weird warmup + 429 race in staging: sample-app warmup probe got a 429 back, SDK retried immediately and we ended up with two signup side-effects.

kira: Oof. So warmup probe retried like a normal request and triggered side-effects?

sam: Yeah. Sequence: first probe -> 429 (quota spike) -> SDK retry without jitter because warmup path replays last request -> server eventually accepted both.

mira: Can you paste minimal curl repro?

sam: curl -X POST https://staging.api.redwood.ai/signup -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -H 'X-Request-Id: warmup-abc' -d '{"email":"staging-warmup@example.com"}'

alex: Two orthogonal problems: (1) warmup probes should not cause side-effects, (2) SDK retry/backoff logic for warmup should be safer (jitter + opt-out).

jen: Agreed. For (1) we can add X-Warmup: true header so backend can short-circuit mutations. For (2) SDKs should treat warmup replays as probes and either skip idempotency header or use unique id so server doesn't dedupe them as the same user action.

kira: Billing concern: if warmup gets billed as normal traffic customers may be unhappy. We need a telemetry label warmup=true to exclude from cost dashboards.

infra-bot: infra note: we already have a dedupe middleware but it's running after auth and the mutation handler triggers side-effects early in some flows. Moving dedupe earlier would help. Filing INF-820.

sam: Also saw this only when 429 happened. If the SDK had applied jitter/backoff before replaying the warmup, the second accepted request likely wouldn't have coincided. So add a special warmup backoff policy: initial backoff randomized 50-150ms, max 1s.

alex: SDK parity note: JS+Python currently implement warmup replay differently. JS replays immediately, Python uses a small delay. We need consistent opt-in config across SDKs: warmup.enabled (bool), warmup.backoff_policy (enum), warmup.header_name.

mira: UX: default warmup.enabled=false to avoid surprising customers. Sample-app templates should not call production mutations during init. Provide a warmup_runner script that hits a read-only health endpoint for prewarm.

jen: Suggested header names and metrics: X-Warmup, X-SDK-Warmup (internal), metric tags: warmup=true, warmup_probe=true, warmup_cost_exempt.

kira: For billing, we'll need a blacklist at the metering pipeline or flag in usage events. I'll own that change (billing task BILL-142).

infra-bot: INF-820 created: dedupe earlier in pipeline + respect X-Warmup header. Owner: @infra.

sam: I'll draft SDK change: add warmup option plus safer backoff. Quick pseudocode:
```
if config.warmup.enabled:
  headers[config.warmup.header_name] = '1'
  // use unique id so we don't accidentally dedupe as real request
  headers['X-Request-Id'] = generate_unique()
  backoff = random_between(50,150)ms on first retry
else:
  // normal idempotency behaviour
  headers['X-Request-Id'] = provided_id or generate()
```

alex: For sample-apps we should update the quickstart to call /health or a new /warmup-readonly endpoint instead of /signup. Add a badge in the readme reminding "do not call side-effect endpoints during init".

mira: Tests to add: e2e warmup flow where server returns 429 on first probe -> SDK retries with warmup header -> assert no duplicate side-effects and warmup metric emitted.

jen: Ops: add alert on warmup_failure_rate spike (new metric). Also add a dashboard panel showing warmup request volume so infra can tune cache priming.

deploy-bot: staging infra patch queued (INF-820) ; expected deploy tomorrow.

kira: I'll work with billing to strip warmup-tagged events from invoices and surface them separately in usage UI.

sam: I'll open SDK PRs (JS/Python/Go). Requesting reviewers: @mira, @alex.

mira: Thanks. One more note: document safe_replay_window (default 60s) so server dedupe logic knows timeframe to consider duplicates. Add to API docs and SDK config.

alex: TL;DR: add X-Warmup header + warmup telemetry + SDK opt-in with safe jittered backoff + move dedupe earlier. Owners: infra(INF-820), billing(BILL-142), SDK(sam).

jen: Leaving thread open for PR links and infra deploy updates.
